focus: was /wɒz/-/wəz/ vs were /wɜː/-/wə/ · past -ed endings /t/ /d/ /ɪd/ · weak forms & connected speech · full A1 vowel review · full A1 consonant review
focus_ar: was مقابل were والصور الخفيفة، ونهايات الماضي -ed، والكلام المتصل، ومراجعة شاملة لحروف العلة والسواكن في A1
arabic_challenge: Arabic does not reduce vowels in unstressed words, so 'was' and 'were' get pronounced at full strength, which sounds heavy and unnatural. The -ed ending has three sounds and is often given a full extra syllable everywhere ('worked' → 'work-ed').

isolation.instructions: Strong forms: was /wɒz/, were /wɜː/. But in normal speech they WEAKEN: was → /wəz/, were → /wə/. 'I was at home' sounds like 'I wəz at home'. Only stress them for emphasis or contradiction.
isolation.instructions_ar: الصورة القوية was /wɒz/ و were /wɜː/. لكن في الكلام العادي بتخف: was → /wəz/. مانضغط عليهم إلا للتوكيد.

daily_drills.record_this: I was at home yesterday and my brothers were at school. She wasn't very happy, but they weren't sad either.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I was at home' quickly. Does 'was' almost disappear into the sentence?

isolation.instructions: Past -ed has three sounds. After voiceless (k, p, s, sh, ch, f) → /t/: worked. After voiced or a vowel → /d/: played. ONLY after /t/ or /d/ → /ɪd/ (extra syllable): wanted, needed.
isolation.instructions_ar: نهاية -ed لها ٣ أصوات: /t/ بعد المهموس (worked)، /d/ بعد المجهور (played)، و /ɪd/ بمقطع زائد بعد /t/ أو /d/ فقط (wanted).

daily_drills.record_this: Yesterday I worked all day and then watched television. She played outside and I visited my family. We wanted to help but we needed more time.
daily_drills.self_check: Only 'wanted', 'needed', 'started', 'visited' should gain a syllable. Check the others stay short.

isolation.instructions: Function words shrink in real speech: to /tə/, at /ət/, and /ən/, of /əv/, for /fə/, you /jə/. 'Did you' becomes /dɪdʒə/. This is not lazy — it is correct, natural English.
isolation.instructions_ar: الكلمات الوظيفية بتتقلّص في الكلام الحقيقي: to /tə/، and /ən/، of /əv/. و'did you' تبقى /dɪdʒə/. ده مش إهمال — ده الإنجليزي الطبيعي.

sentence_practice: Did you go to school yesterday?
I want to have a cup of tea.
We were waiting for you at home.
daily_drills.record_this: Did you go to school yesterday? I wanted to have a cup of tea and some fish and chips. We were waiting for you at home all evening.
daily_drills.self_check: Say the whole line as one smooth flow. If each word sounds separate and equal, reduce the small words more.

isolation.instructions: Run through every vowel contrast from weeks 1-9, two at a time. Say each pair three times, then check yourself in a mirror for lip shape and jaw position.
isolation.instructions_ar: مراجعة كل حروف العلة من الأسبوع ١ لـ ٩، اتنين اتنين. كل زوج ٣ مرات، وراجع شكل شفايفك وفكك في المراية.
practice: iː/ɪ, æ/e, ʌ/æ, ɔː/ɒ, uː/ʊ, ɜː/ɔː

sentence_practice: I eat it. The bad bed. A cup and a cap.
He caught the cot. The fool is full.
My shirt is short. I buy at the bay.
daily_drills.record_this: I eat it every day. The bad bed is in the small room. He is tall but his shirt is short. I want to buy two now, not later.
daily_drills.self_check: Record all six pairs. Play back — is every pair clearly two DIFFERENT words?

isolation.instructions: Run through every consonant challenge from weeks 1-9: /p/ vs /b/, /θ/ and /ð/, /v/ vs /f/, /w/ vs /v/, /tʃ/ vs /ʃ/, /dʒ/ vs /j/, /ŋ/ vs /n/, and initial clusters.
isolation.instructions_ar: مراجعة كل السواكن الصعبة من الأسبوع ١ لـ ٩، بالإضافة للتجمعات الساكنة في البداية.

sentence_practice: Ben has a pen. Three trees.
The van has a fan. My vest is in the west.
A chip and a ship. Jam, not yam.
daily_drills.record_this: Ben has a pen and I can see three trees. The van has a fan inside. I like jam, not yam. I can sing and I can swim, and I play every day.
daily_drills.self_check: Ask a friend to point at which word of each pair you said. Were they right every time?

challenge_sentences: Yesterday I was at home and my family were with me.
I worked all day and then I watched television.
I can swim but I can't drive.
Did you go to school? I wanted to come with you.
daily_drills.record_this: Yesterday I was at home and my family were with me. I worked all day and then I watched television. I can swim but I can't drive. Did you go to school? I wanted to come with you but I needed more time.
daily_drills.self_check: This line contains almost every A1 challenge. Play it back and mark any sound you want to keep practising.

test_yourself.instructions: This is your A1 pronunciation exit check. Record the whole passage, then compare it with your week-1 day-1 recording. The difference is your progress.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: ده اختبار النطق النهائي للمستوى A1. سجّل النص كله وقارنه بتسجيلك في أول أسبوع — الفرق هو تقدّمك.
test_yourself.passage: Hello! My name is Hana and I am from Egypt. I live in a small house with my family. My father is a teacher and my mother is a nurse. I have one sister and two brothers. Every day I get up at seven, eat breakfast and go to work. I finish at five. I can speak Arabic and English, but I can't speak French. In my free time I like reading, swimming and listening to music. Yesterday I was at home. I worked in the morning and then I watched a film. It cost fifteen pounds, not fifty. Thank you very much — have a great day!

sounds_to_check./p/ vs /b/, /v/ vs /f/, /w/ vs /v/: people, brothers — five, father — work, very
sounds_to_check./θ/ and /ð/: three, thank, thirty — this, father, mother, brothers, with
sounds_to_check./iː/ vs /ɪ/, /æ/ vs /e/, /ʌ/, /ɔː/, /ɜː/: eat, sleep — it, finish — family, bad — bed, seven — much — tall — work
sounds_to_check.third-person and past endings: gets, goes, finishes — worked, watched, wanted
sounds_to_check.can vs can't, -ing, clusters: I can speak / I can't speak — reading, swimming — free, speak, small
sounds_to_check.-teen vs -ty, weak forms: fifTEEN vs FIFty — I wəz at home, went tə work

scoring_guide.90_100: Excellent A1 pronunciation. Every meaning-changing contrast is clear. Ready for A2.
scoring_guide.70_89: Solid A1. A few contrasts slip at speed — note them and keep drilling those two or three.
scoring_guide.50_69: Understandable but several contrasts still merge. Revisit the specific weeks for those sounds before moving on.
scoring_guide.below_50: Work through weeks 1-9 again, one week at a time. Progress is normal but needs the daily recording habit.

for_arabic_speakers: Weak forms are the single biggest step toward sounding fluent. Arabic gives every word full value; English does not.
-ed adds a syllable ONLY after /t/ or /d/ (wanted, needed). Everywhere else it is just /t/ or /d/.
Compare your week-10 recording with week 1. Students are usually surprised by how much has changed.
Any contrast still merging after this week is your personal priority list for A2.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the day-7 passage and keep it. It is your A1 pronunciation baseline for the next level.
